candidates.term: The Alchemist inside the Day Gate
candidates.defline: The Alchemist lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: your closest life keeps a quiet corner of its own.
candidates.reading: You need closeness that leaves you time alone, and a partner has to learn that your silences carry work. Because you sort out your feelings in private before you can speak them, you bring conclusions home more than first reactions. Anyone who reads your quiet as coldness wears you down, and you have learned to explain early that the quiet has nothing to do with them. From your mid-thirties, you share your life with someone who values how you think.
candidates.teaser: You need a partner who respects your inner weather: closeness with breathing space built in. Marriage works as two studies with a shared door.

domain_readings.Love: You need a partner who respects your inner weather: closeness with breathing space built in, marriage as two studies with a shared door. The one who pathologizes your solitude will exhaust you. The one who guards it will keep you. Choose the guard, then open your door on schedule.
domain_readings.Mind: At close range your mind stays private even in love: processing alone, concluding aloud. The partner learns your silences carry work, never distance. Teach them the difference early. Intimacy for you is a practice with a rhythm, and the rhythm is learnable.

candidates.life_chapter: Your home chapter keeps a shut door and a shared one: the adult decades build a household with solitude in the floor plan. Expect love that deepens through respected space. The marriage that lasts will know when to knock, and you will love it for knocking.
candidates.relations: The guarding partner is this seat’s person: someone who protects your solitude like a shared asset, because it is. They will explain you to bewildered relatives. Thank them specifically. Translation is an act of devotion, and they perform it weekly.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the shared door sticks: closeness deferred to the study. Emerge on schedule this week, carrying something to show.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the studies never open: parallel lives, adjacent solitudes. Breach your own door first. They are waiting.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the inner weather becomes the marriage’s climate: two people, one forecast.
candidates.health_line: Your body recharges in solitude and depletes in crowds, even beloved ones: schedule the alone time as marital infrastructure. It keeps the shared time warm.

Love.headline: You love best with time alone built in.
Love.recognition: You want a partner close, and you also want hours each week that belong only to you. Because you work out your feelings alone, you go quiet before a serious talk, and a partner who presses gets less of you. What you need in love is someone who waits for you to come back.
Love.lived: So far the people you have loved have split into two kinds, those who left you alone to think and those who took your silence personally. You have stayed longest with the first kind, and the arguments you remember were mostly about time apart.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties your home settles around a shared rhythm, time together and time apart agreed without a fight. You grow closer to a partner in these years by talking through what you have already thought through alone.

Mind.headline: You think alone and speak once you are sure.
Mind.recognition: For days you turn a problem over before you say a word about it, and you say it only once you have an answer. Because a half-formed thought feels unsafe to you, the people closest to you hear your conclusions without the reasoning. You let a partner further into your thinking than anyone, and even they see only part of it.
Mind.lived: So far your clearest thinking has happened alone, late at night or on long walks, away from the people you live with. More than once you have surprised a partner with a decision you had been working on for weeks in silence.
Mind.ahead: From your mid-thirties your thinking deepens and turns toward a single subject you have circled for years. You share more of the work in progress with a partner in these years, and the work gets better for it.
